clue.text: The widow is in sparkling form!

definitions.text: The widow is in sparkling form!

parts.words: The widow is in sparkling form!
parts.note: the Widow is the nickname of Veuve Clicquot, a famous fizzy wine from northern France, so the widow appears as a sparkling drink

explanation.surface: A bereaved woman is in surprisingly high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparkling form' looks like a description of a lively mood; it is the bubbly drink. Veuve Clicquot (veuve is French for widow) is known in the trade simply as 'the Widow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Veuve Clicquot, nicknamed the Widow, is a celebrated sparkling wine from the Reims region.

clue.text: Transport making time for regular comings and goings

definitions.meaning: a bicycle, a means of getting about

definitions.text: time for regular comings and goings
definitions.meaning: a period in which events recur in a repeating pattern

explanation.surface: Vehicles that run to a regular timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bike is a mode of travel; the same word names a recurring period, like the seasons.

clue.text: Mix-up earns student a gamma, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling an anagram

parts.note: L is for learner, a student driver's plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled paper earns the student a third-class mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A gamma is a low grade in British universities. 'Perhaps' rearranges L plus A GAMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or mixture of different elements.

clue.text: Frustration for a potter — it's as much as a person can take!

definitions.meaning: in snooker, a player potting balls is thwarted when the pocket is already full

definitions.text: as much as a person can take
definitions.meaning: the amount a trouser pocket holds

explanation.surface: A ceramicist's annoyance is all anyone can bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests someone making pots; it is a snooker player potting balls, foiled by a full pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocketful is the quantity fitting in a pocket; split, it describes a full pocket thwarting a snooker shot.

clue.text: The fruit of Frazer's work?

parts.note: J. G. Frazer wrote The Golden Bough, so the fruit of that bough would share its colour

explanation.surface: What did Frazer's research produce?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit of work' suggests results; it is literal fruit on Frazer's Golden Bough, his study of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden apples appear in myth, such as those of the Hesperides, matching the golden bough of Frazer's title.

clue.text: Close to a third of 12

indicators.note: a third of the cross-referenced answer means its first three of nine letters

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer at 12 across in this grid

explanation.surface: Nearly a third of a dozen.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like the number; it points to the answer at 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Close and end both mean the finish or conclusion.

clue.text: No parking in the College grounds — reversed into tree!

indicators.note: reversed tells us the shortened grounds word is read backwards
no means the parking letter is taken away from the grounds word

parts.note: a college's grounds are its campus
P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A driver barred from parking on campus backs into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P from CAMPUS leaves CAMUS, which 'reversed' turns into the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree whose dried berries are used as a spice.

clue.text: The Sun King introduced a system of this kind

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, describing the type of system

indicators.note: introduced means the a is brought inside the sun and king pieces

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Louis XIV, the Sun King, brought in a new regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun King' suggests Louis XIV; it is split into SOL and R, with A introduced. The definition points to the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: The planets orbiting our star form the solar system, so the adjective names that type of system.

clue.text: Paid nothing to maintain soldiers' memorial

indicators.note: to maintain means the paid and nothing pieces hold the soldiers inside them

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so paid gives met
soldiers are men
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Getting a soldiers' memorial kept up for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid nothing' suggests a free service and 'to maintain' sounds like upkeep; 'to maintain' is the container signal, holding the soldiers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake serving as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: Stay on — the French ship is not stopping

parts.note: to stay something is to halt or stop it
le is French for the
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Wait aboard: the French vessel is sailing nonstop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay on' seems to mean remain; 'stay' here is to halt, and 'on' just places the next pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless means continuing endlessly, never halting.

clue.text: Opening left in eastern side of church

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity or chance

explanation.surface: A doorway on the left in the east wall of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, traditionally at the east end.

clue.text: Awkward business to find replacement for hat girl

indicators.note: replacement for means the letters of the hat word are put back in a different order

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Finding a stand-in for a milliner's assistant is a tricky affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacement for' is the anagram signal, applied to a synonym (slang for a hat) rather than printed letters, an older Times liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a predicament forcing a choice between unwelcome options, an awkward situation.

clue.text: High flier is well below par

definitions.meaning: a large bird of prey soaring high in the sky
in golf, a hole completed two strokes under the expected score

explanation.surface: A soaring bird is a golfer's very good score.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of prey flies high; in golf the term means two strokes under par on one hole.

clue.text: Nude convert streaked — church shows patience

indicators.note: convert tells us the letters of nude are changed into a new form

parts.note: to streak is to run naked, so streaked gives ran
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A naked convert dashes past while the congregation shows forbearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' looks like a noun, a new believer; it is the anagram signal turning NUDE into ENDU.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance and patience are both the capacity to bear hardship or delay without giving up.

clue.text: What happens when women let their dresses down

definitions.text: What happens when women let their dresses down

parts.words: What happens when women let their dresses down
parts.note: not lengthening a hem but a low-cut neckline, the dress lowered at the top

explanation.surface: A fashion change in which hemlines drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' suggests lengthening a hem; it is a plunging neckline.
explanation.definitionFit: Décolletage is a low neckline on a dress, revealing the neck and shoulders.

clue.text: Beat the book

definitions.meaning: Lamentations, a book of the Old Testament, is abbreviated this way

explanation.surface: Thrash the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is to thrash someone; Lam. is the short form for the Lamentations of Jeremiah in the Bible.

clue.text: 50 units of power overhead, perhaps — it concentrates the light

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an amp is a unit of electrical current; the clue's plural is loose
a shade such as an awning or canopy is overhead

explanation.surface: Fifty watts of overhead light, with something to focus the beam.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly 'units' gives AMPS, so the S is shared with SHADE, a looseness in the clue as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover fitted round a bulb directs and softens its glow.

clue.text: One dictating had to call for a French-speaker

parts.note: General Franco was the dictator of Spain
to call someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A man giving dictation had to ring for someone fluent in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One dictating' suggests an office boss dictating letters; it is a dictator, Franco.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose language is French, especially in a bilingual country, is called this.

clue.text: Fainted after the Sovereign's parade?

definitions.meaning: Sandhurst officer cadets graduate at the Sovereign's Parade, their passing-out ceremony

explanation.surface: A cadet collapsed after the royal march-past.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sovereign's Parade is the passing-out parade at Sandhurst, Britain's army officer academy.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse unconscious; also to have graduated from military training.

clue.text: Oil lamp goes out in the big city

indicators.note: a lamp that goes out is disordered here, so the letters of oil lamp goes are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oil lamp is extinguished in the metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes out' seems to describe the lamp failing, but 'goes' is part of the fodder and 'out' the anagram signal; read here as the indicator phrase over OIL LAMP GOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalopolis is a huge urban area, a very large conurbation.

clue.text: Refuse to dress on time

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Declining to get dressed punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish or waste.

clue.text: Leaves island

definitions.meaning: a Greek island in the Dodecanese, also spelt Kos

explanation.surface: Departs from the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a long-leaved lettuce and also the Aegean island (Kos) it is named after.

clue.text: Shell that's done for the CO

parts.note: a conch is a large spiral seashell
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An explosive shell that finished off the commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: CO here is a conscientious objector, not a commanding officer; 'done for' is a loose link.
explanation.definitionFit: Conchie is old slang for a conscientious objector, someone refusing military service.

clue.text: Sally grabs member for fortune-telling

indicators.note: grabs means the sally word holds the member word inside it

parts.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden military outrush
a leg is a limb or member of the body

explanation.surface: Sally takes hold of somebody to have her fortune told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; it is a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is divination by drawing lots, a form of soothsaying.

clue.text: Holding pen upside down — it's useless

indicators.note: holding means the it word encloses the pen piece

parts.note: it's gives the letters of it, the 's a link

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the word pen is read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Holding a pen upside down won't get you anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upside down' works because this is a down clue: the pen is read from the bottom up, then 'Holding' puts it inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means incompetent or ineffective.

clue.text: He takes any number of chances

definitions.text: He takes any number of chances

parts.words: He takes any number of chances
parts.note: a British machine that picks winning Premium Bond numbers at random, called by a man's name

explanation.surface: A reckless gambler who never stops taking risks.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE (Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment) draws the winners of UK Premium Bonds, a government savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The random-number machine that picks Premium Bond prizes literally generates numbers by chance.

clue.text: Gets snare smashed to bits

indicators.note: smashed to bits means the letters of snare are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A trap is destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to obtain or receive in return for work.

clue.text: A note by a scholar of Magdalen for a literary society

parts.note: C is a musical note
at Magdalen College, Oxford, a scholar is called a demy

explanation.surface: A Magdalen scholar's annotation for a reading group.
explanation.walkthrough: A demy is the name for a foundation scholar at Magdalen College, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy can be a society of learned people, such as the Académie française for letters.

clue.text: Want the Navy to leave, for sure

indicators.note: to leave means the navy letters depart from the want word

parts.note: to want is to yearn
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Wishing the fleet would go, definitely.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an old word for yes or truly, indeed.

clue.text: One more unnamed player getting early points

definitions.meaning: ..., the placeholder printed on a team sheet for an unnamed player, has its full stops near the start

explanation.surface: A further anonymous player scores in the opening minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' look like a score; they are the full stops in the initials of A. N. Other, the British stand-in name on a team list.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an additional one; split as A. N. Other it is the conventional British name for an unnamed team member.

clue.text: School-leaver's certificate?

parts.note: not a diploma for a pupil finishing school but a permit allowing a boarder temporary leave

explanation.surface: A qualification awarded on finishing school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School-leaver' suggests a graduate; here it is a boarder leaving for a weekend, and the document is the Latin-named permission slip ('let him go out').
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is a permission granted to a boarding pupil or student to be absent for a time.

clue.text: A branch head showing skill

parts.note: a department or branch of an organisation, abbreviated
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: The head of a branch office demonstrates competence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland: NESS appears in place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Adeptness is proficiency or expertise in doing something.
